title: 1813-generation-of-threat-hawkes
universal_lens: The Generation of Threat (GoT) primitive unifies multi-agent interaction chains via a multivariate Hawkes point process. By mapping discrete ball-touches to an immigration-birth branching process, it isolates the causal contribution of individual agents to a collective terminal state (dangerous action), bypassing Markovian spatial limitations through history-dependent intensity kernels.
gsi_mapping: GSI maps the GoT branching matrix to a Bayesian hierarchical model where exponential decay parameters are drawn from team-specific priors. Conformal prediction intervals are constructed around the leave-one-player-out threat expectations, providing rigorous, finite-sample uncertainty quantification for undervalued playmakers whose historical event streams exhibit high indirect branching factors.
gse_mapping: In GSE, the 12-dimensional Hawkes process models situational state transitions during offensive drives. The intensity function dictates the probability of entering high-leverage zones (e.g., red zone) given preceding actions. The branching matrix directly measures how specific personnel groupings and micro-actions catalyze downstream explosive plays, enabling dynamic sequence-credit attribution.

primitives.name: History-Dependent Threat Intensity
primitives.verbatim_quote: Mathematics, equations, assumptions - Intensity: λi(t) = μi + ΣjΣ_{tkj<t} αij exp(-β(t-tkj)); branching matrix Γij = αij/β; stability: spectral radius ρ(Γ) < 1.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \lambda_i(t): conditional intensity (events per second); \mu_i: background rate (s^-1); \alpha_{ij}: excitation magnitude (dimensionless expected offspring count); \beta: decay rate (s^-1); t: time (seconds).
primitives.assumptions: Exponential decay of influence on a seconds-scale; concatenation of distinct games into a single continuous process is statistically harmless due to fast decay.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Spectral radius of the branching matrix \rho(\Gamma) \geq 1, leading to an unstable, explosive process where threat generation diverges without bound.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to GSE drive-state transition probabilities, modeling how past events elevate the instantaneous probability of reaching a scoring position.
layer2.telemetry: Log-likelihood of observed event sequences under the fitted Hawkes parameters.

primitives.name: Causal Interaction Branching Matrix
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Use the **immigration–birth representation**: each touch is an "individual" generating offspring touches/threats; the branching matrix Γ gives expected direct children; (I-Γ)-1 gives expected total descendants (Proposition 2.1).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \Gamma_{ij}: expected number of direct offspring events in dimension j triggered by an event in dimension i (dimensionless); I: identity matrix.
primitives.assumptions: Linearity of the superposition principle in the immigration-birth representation; stationarity of the underlying branching mechanism across the observation window.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity at \det(I - \Gamma) = 0, which corresponds exactly to the instability boundary \rho(\Gamma) = 1, rendering total descendant calculations undefined.

layer2.mapping: Forms the core of GSI's sequence-credit engine, mathematically separating direct assists from deep, multi-touch creative contributions.
layer2.telemetry: Weighted MAPE of recovered \Gamma matrices in synthetic simulation studies.

primitives.name: Counterfactual Threat Attribution
primitives.verbatim_quote: - GoTdiri = Γ_{threat,i}; GoTindi = [(I-Γ)-1]_{threat,i}; GoT90,i = GoTdiri × E[touchesi]; GoT90,i = E[threats] - E[threats | row/col i of (K, μ) zeroed].
primitives.latex: GoT90^{LOPO}_i = E[\text{threats}] - E[\text{threats} \mid \text{row/col } i \text{ of } (K, \mu) \text{ zeroed}]
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: GoT90^{LOPO}_i: marginal threat contribution per 90 minutes (dimensionless count); E[threats]: expected total threat events generated by the system.
primitives.assumptions: The counterfactual removal of a player entirely zeroes their incoming and outgoing interaction weights without inducing compensatory structural shifts in remaining players.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Highly collinear tactical systems where removing one node causes massive redistribution of \alpha_{jk} weights among remaining nodes, violating the static counterfactual assumption.

layer2.mapping: Directly implements GSI's 'hidden threat generator' metric, identifying players whose absence structurally collapses the team's overall threat generation capacity.
layer2.telemetry: Variance of GoT90 estimates derived via parametric bootstrap over MLE parameter distributions.

reasoning_traces.think:
The Generation of Threat (GoT) framework fundamentally restructures sports analytics by abandoning Markovian state-space assumptions in favor of a history-dependent Hawkes point process. The derivation begins by defining a 12-dimensional event stream: 11 dimensions representing ball touches by players in specific formation positions, and the 12th dimension capturing 'threat events' (entry into a predefined danger zone). The core mathematical operator is the conditional intensity function, \lambda_i(t), which posits that the instantaneous rate of an event is driven by a baseline exogenous rate plus the cumulative, exponentially decaying influence of all prior endogenous events. This structure elegantly maps to an immigration-birth branching process. In this dual representation, every ball touch acts as an ancestor that stochastically generates offspring touches or terminal threats. The expected number of direct offspring is captured by the branching matrix \Gamma, where elements \Gamma_{ij} = \alpha_{ij}/\beta quantify the causal strength from position/player i to j. To attribute credit beyond immediate predecessors, the framework employs the Neumann series expansion of the resolvent matrix (I - \Gamma)^{-1}. This matrix yields the expected total descendants, effectively summing infinite-order interaction chains. The ultimate sovereign primitive is the leave-one-player-out counterfactual metric (GoT90 LOPO), which calculates the exact drop in expected threat events if a specific player's interaction rows and columns are zeroed. Failure modes emerge primarily when the spectral radius \rho(\Gamma) approaches unity, indicating an unstable, explosive system where small perturbations yield infinite threat expectations. Furthermore, the counterfactual metric assumes structural rigidity; if removing a player drastically alters the tactical topology (redistribution of passing weights), the static subtraction introduces bias.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: The GoT primitive inherits its mathematical DNA from the foundational theory of self-exciting point processes introduced by Hawkes (1971) in seismology to model aftershocks. The specific use of exponential kernels and the immigration-birth duality was rigorously formalized by Ogata (1981, 1988) for maximum likelihood estimation. In quantitative finance, similar branching structures were adapted by Embrechts et al. to model high-frequency trading cascades and market crashes. The translation to sports analytics represents a novel application of these stochastic epidemic models, moving performance evaluation from static box scores to dynamic, network-based causal inference.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Within the GoT framework, opposing agents—specifically the defending team—are not modeled as active strategic optimizers but rather as environmental constraints that define the terminal 'threat' state. The defensive pressure is implicitly encoded in the baseline intensity \mu and the suppression of certain transition probabilities \alpha_{ij}. However, the model inherently assumes that the attacking players' decision-making (the choice of whom to pass to) follows a stationary stochastic policy conditioned only on the recent history of touches. It abstracts away the explicit cognitive state of defenders, treating them as a static geometric boundary (the danger zone) rather than adaptive agents actively minimizing the branching factor \Gamma.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: To prevent leakage and anti-collinearity between layers, strict data-processing rules must be enforced. First, set-piece crosses are explicitly excluded to avoid inflating the branching factors of designated takers who operate outside open-play tactical networks. Second, opponent possession times are aggressively compressed (e.g., to ~12 seconds) to ensure the temporal continuity of the Hawkes process is not artificially broken by long, irrelevant dead-ball states. Third, the formation clustering must remain stable; if a player frequently switches positions, their dimensional mapping becomes ambiguous, causing cross-talk in the \Gamma matrix. Finally, a minimum sample size (e.g., 600 minutes of reliable exposure) is mandated to ensure the MLE of the exponential kernels converges and the spectral radius remains safely below the singularity threshold.
